purpose: Lists the values of one entitlement code map, paged and filtered.

params.name: id
params.values: code map id, Base64-encoded (the server decodes it before the lookup)

params.name: q
params.values: '*' returns all values; a value starting or ending with '*' is used as given; anything else is searched as *value*. Default 'default' (so it searches *default*)

answer: {nextIndex:int, arraySize:int, hasMore:bool, codeMapValues:[{id, value, displayLabel, description, nativeValue}]}
notes: id is the Base64 of the code map key, which is the entitlement view's viewID (the escaped GUID string from POST /catalog/drivers/driver, e.g. \97\64\89…). The entitlement DN or name, Base64-encoded, answered arraySize 0. An unknown id is not an error (200, arraySize 0); a blank id gives 489. value is the compact JSON a resource stores; nativeValue is the connected system's own key.

purpose: Starts a code map refresh for every resource-mapped entitlement of the given drivers.

fields.name: drivers
fields.values: list of driver objects; required (an empty list fails with 'no drivers found')

fields.name: drivers[].id
fields.values: driver DN, or the literal 'ALL DRIVERS' in the first entry to refresh every available driver

notes: Refreshes the code maps of the driver's resource-mapping entitlements by querying the connected system through the driver (a running driver is needed). A query entitlement succeeded; a fixed-value one is listed under failed with 'Unable to complete codemap refresh' (it has no code map, which is expected). The driver key is 'id', not 'dn'. If a refresh is already in progress the call returns at once with that entity listed under succeeded and an in-progress reason. Also flushes the driver and entitlement-value caches.

purpose: Starts a code map refresh for the listed entitlements.

fields.name: entitlements
fields.values: list of entitlement objects; an empty or missing list does nothing and answers with no body

notes: Entitlement key is 'id'. Refreshes that entitlement's code map through the driver. Stops at the first entitlement whose refresh is already in progress and answers with just that one. Flushes caches first.

purpose: Lists the first-level sub-containers under a root (a read despite POST).

fields.name: dn
fields.values: container to list under; wins over everything else

fields.name: level
fields.values: role level number; lists under that level's container; with level 20 the 'System' sub-container is left out

fields.name: type
fields.values: only 'resource' (any case) is checked: lists resource-definition containers under the resource root

fields.name: searchScope
fields.values: 'o'/'one' (one level, the default) or 's'/'subtree'; anything else is 489

example: POST …/containers/container {} → o=data with devices, groups, sa, users
notes: An empty body lists under the user entity's search root (lab: o=data). The dashboard sends {} (users), {id:'',type:'resource'} (resources) and {dn:<role root>} (roles). type 'role' or 'prd' is not special and falls back to the user root. Values are XSS-checked (400).

purpose: Returns the root container that holds provisioning request definitions.
notes: No parameters. The dashboard's catalog pickers use it as the starting point for /containers/container.

purpose: Returns the root container that holds resource definitions.
notes: No parameters. The dashboard's catalog pickers use it as the starting point for /containers/container.

purpose: Returns the root container that holds role definitions.
notes: No parameters. The dashboard's catalog pickers use it as the starting point for /containers/container.

purpose: Counts roles, resources or users (one kind per call).

params.name: clientId
params.values: dashboard client configuration id; defaults to 1 (lab: 1)

notes: Only one kind is counted even when several flags are true: roles first, then resources, then users. With all flags false the server raises 'Please choose entities to get the count', which reaches the client as a 500 HTML error page. Users are counted in the client's users-list container and capped (hasMore true when the cap is hit) unless VLV counting is on. The lab answered 0 for roles and resources although system roles exist. Dashboard sends users=true&clientId=<client>.

purpose: Exports the workflow database for migration as a zip file.
answer: application/zip, Content-Disposition attachment; filename="wf_db_migration.zip": one <TABLE>/<n>.json file per workflow table (AFACTIVITY, AFCOMMENT, AFDOCUMENT, AFENGINE, AFENGINESTATE, AFFORM, AFMODEL, AFPROCESS, AFPROVISIONINGSTATUS, AFWORKTASK, CONFIGURATION, LOCALIZATION), each {"<TABLE>": [rows]} with lower-case column names; large tables are split into 1.json, 2.json, …
notes: Exports the workflow engine's database tables for migration. Only while the workflow engine is stopped: on a running engine the answer is an HTML 500 (server log: 'Workflow data migration is not possible, since the engine is in running state.'). With the engine stopped the export took 0.4 s (425 KB, 14 files, on a small lab). Send Accept: application/zip; Accept: application/json gets 406. The CONFIGURATION table carries the workflow settings, including the email-based approval account's password setting (empty on the lab; whether a set value is exported in clear was not seen), so treat the file as sensitive. Requires a provisioning administrator. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Imports a workflow migration file.

body.example: multipart/form-data with part 'file' = the exported zip

fields.name: file
fields.values: multipart form part with the exported migration file

notes: Imports a workflow export (multipart/form-data, part 'file' = the zip from GET …/data/migration/workflow). Only with the workflow engine stopped (as for the export). Importing a fresh export of the same system: 200 with no body in under a second; afterwards the processes kept their ids, but the open tasks got new task ids (same addressees), and GET …/admin/workflowengines showed the new engine 'Starting' until the applications were restarted. Requires a provisioning administrator. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Lists the Directory Abstraction Layer entity definitions, or one by key.

params.name: key
params.values: entity key; returns that one definition instead of the list

params.name: clientId
params.values: dashboard client configuration id; defaults to 1 (lab: 1)

params.name: creatable
params.values: true to keep only creatable entities

params.name: editable
params.values: true to keep only editable ones

params.name: removable
params.values: true to keep only removable ones

params.name: viewable
params.values: true to keep only viewable ones

answer: {entities:[{key, editKey, display, isCreatable, isEditable, isViewable, isRemovable, namingAttribute, attributes:[{key, displayLabel, dataType, isSearchable, isRequired, isEditable, isMultivalued, formatType, lookupEntity?, choiceList?…}]}], totalCount:int}; with key: one entity object
notes: Lab has 54 definitions (user, group, container, quick-user-info, user-lookup, many sys-*). An unknown key gives 489 'Internal Error'. The dashboard uses creatable=true&viewable=true for its entity list (lab: group and user) and key=group&clientId=… for group attributes. Errors seen on the lab: an unknown key (key=nosuch) → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.' rather than a not-found message.

purpose: Reads chosen attributes of a list of entities by DN (a read despite POST).

params.name: filterAttr
params.values: comma-separated attribute keys to return; without it only the dn comes back

notes: Missing entityKey: 'Entity key cannot be empty'. Missing userList: 'User dn is not found in the request payload'. A DN that is not of the given entity also gives that message. Not used by the dashboard. Errors seen on the lab: {} → 489 'Entity key cannot be empty'; entityKey=user with filterAttr and a dns list → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'; entityKey=group with userList → 489 'User dn is not found in the request payload.'.

purpose: Create a directory object of any creatable entity (user, group, …) from its entity definition.

fields.name: key
fields.values: entity key from GET /access/entities/definitions with isCreatable true (lab: user, group, sys-…)

fields.name: attributes
fields.values: list of {key, attributeValues:[…]}; every attribute the definition marks required needs a value, else 489 'Attribute: <name> is required'

fields.name: attributes[key=container]
fields.values: container of the new object; without it the client's configured container is used

fields.name: attributes[key=cn]
fields.values: naming value; with the container it makes the DN

notes: Also creates a user WITHOUT a password (key user, FirstName and LastName required on the lab): the way to get a scratch user when POST /access/user is refused by the password policy. Same DN again: 489 EntityAlreadyExist. It only creates: a body {key, dn} meant as a read answered 489 'Attribute: Container is required'. Errors seen on the lab: a group without the required Description → 489 'Attribute: Description is required'; the same cn again → 489 'Entity ID already exists. Specify a different Entity ID.'.

notes: Change visible at once in GET /catalog/groups.

purpose: Searches objects of one DAL entity, paged, or reads one object by DN.

params.name: searchKeys
params.values: comma-separated attribute keys to search and show; needed when the client has no entity configuration for this key

params.name: entityDN
params.values: returns just that object (with filterAttr attributes)

params.name: isDynamic
params.values: 'true' searches with the definition's searchable attributes when no configuration exists; default false

params.name: isOrgChart
params.values: 'true' uses the org-chart display attributes; default false

params.name: lookupAttr
params.values: 'true' also returns lookup attributes; default false

params.name: advSearch
params.values: ';'-separated key:value terms (e.g. FirstName:a*;LastName:b*); keys must be searchable, non-time attributes

params.name: sortBy
params.values: attribute key; must be one of the entity's display attributes

params.name: clientId
params.values: dashboard client configuration id; defaults to 1 (lab: 1)

answer: {entityList:[{dn, attributes:[{key, displayLabel, attributeValues:[…], dataType, …}]}], nextIndex (-1 = no more), totalCount, hasMore}; with entityDN+filterAttr: {entityList:[{dn, attributes:[{key, attributeValues:[{@type:'entityInfoNode', dn, name, type}]}]}]}
notes: With searchKeys the rows carry only those attributes; with isDynamic=true all the entity's display attributes (Department, Email, FirstName, …). Paging: size=2 gave nextIndex 3, totalCount 3. entityDN + filterAttr reads DN-valued attributes of one object, resolved to names: filterAttr=directReports on the manager listed both reports; filterAttr=manager,group on Alice gave her manager and her group (comma-separated keys work). entityKey=group with searchKeys=Description listed both groups; searchKeys=cn for groups gave 489 'Internal Error' (use an attribute the definition has; cn is not one for group). sortBy FirstName or LastName: 489 'Sort column is not specified as entity display attribute' (no per-client entity configuration on the lab, so no display attributes to sort by). With no per-client entity configuration (dashboard Configuration > Entities) and neither searchKeys nor isDynamic, the server answers 489 'Entity configuration is missing'. sys-nrf-role with searchKeys=cn also gave 'Internal Error'. Errors seen on the lab: no entityKey → 489 'Entity key cannot be empty'; entityKey=group with searchKeys=cn → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'; sortBy on a column that is not a display attribute → 489 'Sort column is not specified as entity display attribute'; entityKey=group on the lab → 489 'Entity configuration is missing'.
evidence: live 2026-10-30 (test users, groups and a team)

purpose: Creates a user and optionally sets the password.

fields.name: container
fields.values: container DN; default is the configured user root container

fields.values: list of attributes; at least one required

fields.values: attribute key from the user entity; the naming attribute (cn) value plus container makes the DN

fields.values: list of strings; time values as epoch milliseconds, binary (UserPhoto) as Base64 of a valid image

fields.values: if true the first value must be non-empty

notes: Creates a user with an initial password. Every attribute needs isRequired (true or false): without it the server fails with 489 'Internal Error' (a null pointer in the server log). The password must meet the password policy that applies to the new user, which is per installation: on the lab a 15-character password was refused with 489 'Cannot create the user. The password does not meet the password policy criteria.' (subcode errorResponseDuringNmasPasswordMgmt; the lab's policy allows at most 12) and a 12-character one with upper and lower case, digits and two special characters worked; no password at all gave the same refusal. The new user could then sign in with the OSP password grant. A user without a password can be created with POST /access/entities/item key=user. An existing DN gives 489 existing-user. Values are XSS-checked (400).

purpose: Says whether a user is a domain or delegated administrator of a domain.

params.name: level
params.values: 1 = domain administrator (default), 2 = delegated administrator; anything else is 489

params.name: type
params.values: domain, any case: ROLES, COMPLIANCE, PROVISIONING, RBPM-APP, SECURITY (checked); RESOURCES is accepted but always false; PRD, CONFIGURATION, ATTESTATION, SOD, TEAMS, RBPM are rejected

notes: The reference lists PRD as a type, but the server only accepts PROVISIONING for that domain. Missing type: 'Value for type is either invalid or not supported'. Lab uaadmin, level 1: ROLES/COMPLIANCE/PROVISIONING/RBPM-APP true, SECURITY false. Not used by the dashboard. Errors seen on the lab: no userDN → 489 'Value for userDN is missing in payload…'; no type → 489 'Value for type is either invalid or not supported…'; level=3 → 489 'Value for level is either invalid or not supported…'.

purpose: Moves or renames a user's DN through the workflow engine.
notes: Despite the name, it changes the user's DN only in the workflow database (for after a user was renamed or moved in the directory); the directory entry is not touched. It answered 200 for an existing user (who kept the old DN in the directory) and also for a DN that does not exist. Only a provisioning administrator may call it; others get 400 (security error mapped to the XSS code). Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Clears the DirXML-EntitlementResult attribute on a user.
notes: Clears the user's DirXML-EntitlementResult. A user without one: {isSuccess:false, message:'Attribute:DirXML-EntitlementResult  not found on the user dn:…'}. Missing userDn: 489 'Invalid input DN: null'. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Returns the signed-in user's basic details as configured for the client (header card, profile).

params.name: clientId
params.values: dashboard client configuration id; defaults to 1 (lab: 1)

params.name: isProfile
params.values: true for the My Profile page attribute set; default false

answer: {dn, fullName, canHide, imageAttr, primaryAttributes, secondaryAttributes, otherAttributes, disabledLogin, disabledLoginSupported, helpdeskDetails, isHelpdeskUser, teamManger, hideProfilePhoto}
notes: Always about the caller; no DN parameter. Note the field spelled teamManger.

purpose: Searches users whose request history the caller may view (helpdesk).

params.name: columnCustomization
params.values: 'true' applies the manage-users column customization; default false

params.name: clientId
params.values: dashboard client configuration id; defaults to 1 (lab: 1)

answer: {usersList:[same rows as /users/list], nextIndex (-1 = no more)}; with searchCount=true {nextIndex, totalCount}
notes: Same rows as GET /access/users/list, but the answer has no totalSize. isHistory true or false made no difference here. Paging size=2 gave nextIndex 3. sortBy LastName/FirstName with desc sorted correctly. q=Alice found Alice. Callers who are neither domain administrators nor helpdesk users for a client get an unauthorized error. Not used by the dashboard.
evidence: live 2026-10-30 (test users, groups and a team)

purpose: Searches people in the user search root with the dashboard's display columns.

params.name: q
params.values: text matched against names; * or empty for all

params.name: sortBy
params.values: a directory attribute key of the user entity, e.g. LastName, FirstName, Title

params.name: searchAttr
params.values: attribute key to search instead of names, e.g. Title

params.name: columnCustomization
params.values: true leaves the attribute columns out

answer: {usersList:[{dn, fullName, canHide, imageAttr, primaryAttributes:[{key, displayLabel, attributeValues:[{@type, $}], …}], secondaryAttributes, disabledLogin, disabledLoginSupported, isHelpdeskUser, teamManger, hideProfilePhoto}], nextIndex (-1 = no more), totalSize}; with searchCount=true only {nextIndex, totalCount, totalSize}
notes: With users present: primaryAttributes carried Department and Title and secondaryAttributes Email and TelephoneNumber (the client's quick-info columns; per installation), with values only where the user has them. q matches names (Manager found the manager; dctest-a found nothing); searchAttr=Title with q='Test Analyst' found the one user with that title. sortBy works on directory attributes (LastName desc, FirstName asc, Title all sorted correctly); an unknown attribute gives 489 'Sort on Bogus does not work. Please check your Directory Abstraction Layer configuration'. Paging: size=2 gave nextIndex 3; totalSize is the whole count. searchCount=true returns the count alone (totalCount 3) and no list. columnCustomization=true dropped primaryAttributes and secondaryAttributes from each row.
evidence: live 2026-10-30 (test users, groups and a team)
